title: Northern Sea of Galilee and Bethsaida
scope: A source-based evidence study, not an ancient terrain reconstruction. Modern site reference points locate competing identifications; the available reports do not supply reusable, georeferenced ancient shorelines or river courses.

periods.label: 1st century CE
periods.summary: A viewing interval for evidence associated with the early Roman landscape. Some reported occupation and lake-level estimates span a wider period.

periods.label: Byzantine period
periods.summary: A broad regional viewing interval, not a claim that every feature existed throughout these four centuries.

sites.name: El-Araj
sites.coordinateMeaning: Modern reference point for the candidate site, not a surveyed excavation feature.

sites.name: Et-Tell
sites.coordinateMeaning: Modern reference point for the candidate site, not a surveyed excavation feature.
sites.interpretation: Proposed identification with Bethsaida; disputed. Byzantine occupation was not assessed in this pilot.

claims.title: Roman occupation at El-Araj
claims.text: The 2017 team reported 1st–3rd-century pottery, a Nero denarius dated 65–66 CE, and bathhouse remains. A Roman wall was recorded at −211.16 m relative to the report's sea-level reference.
claims.uncertainty: The occupation range extends beyond the selected century. A wall elevation is not a water-level measurement; the report does not identify a geoid or survey benchmark.

claims.title: Roman occupation at Et-Tell
claims.text: The Et-Tell project reports Hellenistic and Roman remains and fishing equipment. It favors identifying this inland site with Bethsaida and proposes changes to the ancient shoreline.
claims.uncertainty: The identification and shoreline explanation remain debated. No precise ancient shoreline geometry is imported from this account.

claims.title: Competing Roman lake-level interpretations
claims.text: Giaime and Artzy infer an early Roman highstand around −208 to −209 m MSL. The El-Araj team argues for lower water from remains below that range.
claims.uncertainty: Different sites, dates, assumptions and vertical references must be reconciled before either interpretation can define an ancient shoreline.

claims.title: Sedimentation and later occupation
claims.text: The excavation team associates river-deposited mud and clay with an occupation gap around 250–350 CE and reports subsequent Byzantine settlement.
claims.uncertainty: This local stratigraphic interpretation supplies neither a regional flood boundary nor a georeferenced former Jordan channel.

claims.title: Byzantine church
claims.text: The 2019 expedition reported a Byzantine church with mosaic floors, marble chancel-screen material and gilded tesserae. Its proposed connection to Willibald's pilgrimage account is an interpretation.
claims.uncertainty: A church and later pilgrimage tradition do not establish the location of an apostle's 1st-century house.

claims.title: Earlier walls beneath the church
claims.text: The 2024 team dated walls east of the church to the late 4th or early 5th century using pottery. It proposed an earlier sacred compound associated with the Peter tradition.
claims.uncertainty: The report notes the absence of well-contextualized coins for this dating; the sacred-compound interpretation is a hypothesis.

claims.title: A Byzantine water-level constraint at Kursi
claims.text: Giaime and Artzy use a fishpond's circulation surface at −213.84 m MSL as a maximum mean lake-level constraint during construction in the 5th–6th centuries.
claims.uncertainty: An upper bound at a dated structure is neither a constant water surface for the entire Byzantine period nor a reconstructed coastline.

waterLevelAlternatives.label: Early Roman highstand proposal
waterLevelAlternatives.datum: MSL as reported by Giaime and Artzy; no transformation to the selected terrain provider's vertical reference has been established.
waterLevelAlternatives.applicability: Broad Late Hellenistic / Early Roman interpretation, challenged by evidence interpreted differently at El-Araj.

waterLevelAlternatives.label: El-Araj Roman wall elevation
waterLevelAlternatives.datum: 211.16 metres below sea level in the excavation report; benchmark and geoid are unspecified.
waterLevelAlternatives.applicability: An archaeological find elevation. It must not be offered as a lake-level preset.

waterLevelAlternatives.label: Kursi construction-time upper bound
waterLevelAlternatives.datum: MSL as reported from differential GPS measurements; compatibility with the current DEM and Cesium ellipsoidal heights has not been established.
waterLevelAlternatives.applicability: Maximum mean level inferred for a 5th–6th-century construction context at Kursi, not a dated full-lake shoreline.

shoreline.reason: No openly reusable, georeferenced epoch-specific shoreline geometry was located in the reviewed sources. This is a scoped research result, not a claim that no such data exists.

riverCourses.reason: Local sediment evidence is insufficient to draw a precise former Jordan channel.

ancientTerrain.reason: Modern topography does not recover buried surfaces, past delta sedimentation, tectonic displacement or lake bathymetry.

renderingRules: Show candidate identifications and report authors explicitly; do not silently select a single Bethsaida location.
Date filters select evidence relevant to a viewing interval; they do not establish continuous occupation or the absence of unindexed evidence.
Preserve the distinction between find elevations, inferred water-level intervals and upper bounds.
Any modern DEM height screen is an uncalibrated illustration unless vertical references are harmonized. It is not a historical waterline or a hydraulic inundation model.
Do not use find elevations as water-level presets.
Do not generate ancient coastline polygons, river paths, excavation footprints, buildings or numerical uncertainty radii from these reference points.
Retain source credits and direct links when displaying these claims.
